payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear definition of a normal reading paradigm as a reading task where participants read sentences without a specific annotation goal, contrasting it with a task-specific reading paradigm where participants search for semantic relations.

claims.text: A normal reading paradigm involves participants reading sentences without a specific task, focusing on passive reading.
In the normal reading paradigm, participants read 349 sentences, contrasting with 390 sentences in a task-specific reading paradigm.
The normal reading paradigm allows for the comparison of cognitive processing during natural reading versus annotation tasks.
